import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 124

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/124](https://www.erdosproblems.com/124)
- [BEGL96] Burr, S. A. and Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Li, W. Wen-Ching, Complete sequences of sets of integer powers. Acta Arith. (1996), 133-138.
-/

open Filter
open scoped Pointwise

namespace Erdos124

/-- The set of integers which are the sum of distinct powers `d ^ i` with `i ≥ k`. -/
def sumsOfDistinctPowers (d k : ℕ) : Set ℕ :=
  {x | ∃ s : Finset ℕ, (∀ i ∈ s, k ≤ i) ∧ ∑ i ∈ s, d ^ i = x}

/--
Let  $3 \le d_1 < d_2 < \dots < d_r$ be integers such that
$$\sum_{1 \le i \le r}\frac 1{d_i - 1} \ge 1.$$
Can all sufficiently large integers be written as a sum of the shape $\sum_i c_ia_i$
where $c_i \in \{0, 1\}$ and $a_i$ has only the digits $0, 1$ when written in base $d_i$?

Conjectured by Erdős [Er97], solved by Boris Alexeev using Aristotle.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
lemma erdos124.zero : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ D : Finset ℕ, (∀ d ∈ D, 3 ≤ d) → 1 ≤ ∑ d ∈ D, (d - 1 : ℚ)⁻¹ →
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, n ∈ ∑ d ∈ D, sumsOfDistinctPowers d 0 := sorry

/--
Let $k \ne 0$ and $3\leq d_1 < d_2 < \cdots < d_r$ be integers of gcd equal to $1$ such that
$$\sum_{1 \le i \le r}\frac 1{d_i - 1} \ge 1.$$
Can all sufficiently large integers be written as a sum of the shape $\sum_i c_ia_i$
where $c_i \in \{0, 1\}$ and $a_i$ is divisible by $d_i ^ k$ and has only the digits $0, 1$ when
written in base $d_i$?

Conjectured by Burr, Erdős, Graham, and Li [BEGL96]
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
lemma erdos124.ne_zero : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ k ≠ 0, ∀ D : Finset ℕ, (∀ d ∈ D, 3 ≤ d) → 1 ≤ ∑ d ∈ D, (d - 1 : ℚ)⁻¹ → D.gcd id = 1 →
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, n ∈ ∑ d ∈ D, sumsOfDistinctPowers d k := by
  sorry

/--
All sufficiently large integers can be written as $a + b + c$, where $a$, $b$, and $c$ are
divisible by $3$, $4$, and $7$ respectively, and after division by that base have only the
digits $0, 1$ in that base.

Proved by Burr, Erdős, Graham, and Li [BEGL96]
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
lemma erdos124.ne_zero_three_four_seven :
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      n ∈ sumsOfDistinctPowers 3 1 + sumsOfDistinctPowers 4 1 + sumsOfDistinctPowers 7 1 :=
  sorry

/--
Let $3\leq d_1 < d_2 < \cdots < d_r$ be integers such that all sufficiently large integers can be
written as a sum of the shape $\sum_i c_ia_i$ where $c_i \in \{0, 1\}$ and $a_i$ has only the digits
$0, 1$ when written in base $d_i$. Then
$$\sum_{1 \le i \le r}\frac 1{d_i - 1} \ge 1.$$

Reported by Burr, Erdős, Graham, and Li [BEGL96] as an observation of Pomerance
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/arex1337/formal-conjectures-proofs/blob/3b7d581c75fd00e482deabfb20675cf3ccfaf49f/Erdos124/Converse.lean"]
lemma erdos124.converse {D : Finset ℕ} (hD₃ : ∀ d ∈ D, 3 ≤ d)
    (h : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, n ∈ ∑ d ∈ D, sumsOfDistinctPowers d 0) : 1 ≤ ∑ d ∈ D, (d - 1 : ℚ)⁻¹ :=
  sorry

/--
For any $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists an infinite sequence $2 \le d_0 < d_1 < \dots$ such
that all sufficiently large integer can be written as $\sum_{i \in I} a_i$ where $a_i$ has only
the digits $0, 1$ when written in base $d_i$,
but $\sum_{i \in I} \frac 1{d_i - 1} \le \varepsilon$.

Proved by Melfi [Me04]
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
lemma erdos124.melfi_construction {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ d : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono d ∧ ∑' i, (d i - 1 : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ ε ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      ∃ (I : Finset ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ i ∈ I, a i ∈ sumsOfDistinctPowers (d i) 0) ∧
        ∑ i ∈ I, a i = n :=
  sorry

end Erdos124

findings.description: The cutoff `0` in `sumsOfDistinctPowers (d i) 0` makes the entire representability condition automatic for every sequence d: take `I = Finset.range n` and `a i = 1`, using exponent 0 at each selected base. This does not express Melfi's positive-power completeness. The difference persists after repairing both the base bound and summability: I proved in Lean that d(i)=2^(i+2) has a convergent reciprocal series bounded by 1 and satisfies the coded representation condition, but fails completeness at cutoff 1 because every permitted sum is even.
findings.source_evidence: Melfi, On certain positive integer sequences, §4, Proposition 1 (https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0404555; TeX source https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0404555), requires '(ii) for every s≥1, Pow(A;s) is complete.' Immediately beforehand, Pow(A;s) is defined using powers a^k with k≥s. The proof explicitly notes that the constructed A does not depend on s.
findings.suggested_fix: After choosing d and imposing its reciprocal-series conditions, require `∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∃ (I : Finset ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ i ∈ I, a i ∈ sumsOfDistinctPowers (d i) k) ∧ ∑ i ∈ I, a i = n`. Update the docstring to describe positive exponent cutoffs. A separately intended k=1 specialization would also avoid the triviality; k=0 does not capture the construction.

findings.description: The real-valued bound `∑' i, (d i - 1 : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ ε` lacks a summability requirement. In Mathlib, a nonsummable real series has `tsum = 0`. Consequently d(i)=i+2 passes this bound for every positive ε, although its reciprocal series is the divergent harmonic series ∑ 1/(i+1). Together with the cutoff-zero representation, this yields a short Lean proof of the entire current declaration without Melfi's construction. Strict monotonicity and even the missing lower bound on bases do not prevent this witness.
findings.source_evidence: Melfi, §4, Proposition 1(i), requires `∑_{a∈A} 1/(a−1) < ε`. Its proof constructs A={p+1}∪{n²p:n≥1} and explicitly bounds the convergent series `1/p + ∑_{n=1}∞ 1/(n²p−1)` by ε (https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0404555). This is a genuinely small convergent series, not a default value for divergence.
findings.suggested_fix: Under `∃ d`, add `Summable (fun i => (d i - 1 : ℝ)⁻¹)` alongside the existing bound. Alternatively, express the bound using nonnegative extended-real sums or bounded finite partial sums, together with the valid-base restriction.

findings.description: The statement requires only `StrictMono d`, omitting `2 ≤ d 0`. Thus bases 0 and 1 are allowed. This matters independently of the other defects: `sumsOfDistinctPowers 1 k = Set.univ` for every k, since any n is a sum of n distinct exponents of base 1; meanwhile the reciprocal contribution of base 1 is `(1−1)⁻¹ = 0`. I proved in Lean that the strictly increasing sequence (1,4,8,16,...) has a convergent reciprocal series bounded by 1 and satisfies completeness for every cutoff k solely through its invalid base 1.
findings.source_evidence: Melfi's Proposition 1 explicitly constructs 'a set A of integers ≥2' (https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0404555, §4). The declaration's own docstring likewise specifies `2 ≤ d₀ < d₁ < …`, but the Lean statement has no corresponding lower bound.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `2 ≤ d 0` to the conjunction under `∃ d`; together with `StrictMono d`, this guarantees every base is at least 2. Equivalently, require `∀ i, 2 ≤ d i` or use a suitably restricted base type.

reformulations.difference: The pointwise sum of the sets of power sums does not explicitly include the source's outer coefficients c_i∈{0,1}.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every `sumsOfDistinctPowers d k` contains 0 via the empty exponent set. Thus a zero coefficient can be absorbed by selecting 0 from that set, and a coefficient of one leaves the selected element unchanged. Conversely every pointwise-sum representation gives a coefficient representation by setting all coefficients to one. A generic membership ↔ coefficient-representation lemma was proved for arbitrary D, k, and n; the same argument applies to the other finite sumset statements.

reformulations.difference: Considering only the inequality's strictness, the file uses `≤ ε` whereas Melfi uses `< ε`. This is separate from the defects reported above.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For an existence theorem quantified over every positive ε, the weak-bound version implies the strict-bound version by applying it at ε/2, retaining the same witness and obtaining cost ≤ ε/2 < ε. The converse is immediate. I proved this equivalence for an arbitrary witness predicate and real-valued cost function.

import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«124»

/-! Short demonstrations of the three defects in the stated Melfi construction. -/

open Filter

namespace Erdos124Review

-- Erdos124.erdos124.melfi_construction: cutoff zero represents every n for every sequence,
-- simply by adding n copies of d_i^0 = 1.
theorem cutoff_zero_is_automatic (d : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ (I : Finset ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ),
      (∀ i ∈ I, a i ∈ Erdos124.sumsOfDistinctPowers (d i) 0) ∧ ∑ i ∈ I, a i = n := by
  exact ⟨Finset.range n, fun _ => 1, fun _ _ => ⟨{0}, by simp, by simp⟩, by simp⟩

-- Erdos124.erdos124.melfi_construction: the bases d_i = i+2 have a divergent harmonic
-- reciprocal series, so its real-valued tsum is the default zero, not a small convergent sum.
theorem reciprocal_series_diverges :
    ¬ Summable (fun i : ℕ => (((i + 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) - 1)⁻¹) := by
  have h := mt (summable_nat_add_iff (f := fun i : ℕ => (i : ℝ)⁻¹) 1).mp
    Real.not_summable_natCast_inv
  convert h using 1
  norm_num [Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one, Nat.cast_ofNat, add_sub_assoc]

-- Erdos124.erdos124.melfi_construction: the EXACT original theorem follows from d_i = i+2,
-- because the divergent series has tsum zero and the representation uses only ones.
theorem original_statement_is_trivial : type_of% @Erdos124.erdos124.melfi_construction := by
  intro ε hε
  refine ⟨fun i => i + 2, fun _ _ h => Nat.add_lt_add_right h 2, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [tsum_eq_zero_of_not_summable reciprocal_series_diverges]
    exact hε.le
  · exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall (cutoff_zero_is_automatic _)

-- Erdos124.erdos124.melfi_construction: StrictMono permits the invalid base 1, whose
-- reciprocal term is zero and whose power sums contain every natural at every cutoff.
theorem missing_base_bound :
    StrictMono (fun i : ℕ => i + 1) ∧ ¬ 2 ≤ (fun i : ℕ => i + 1) 0 ∧
      ((1 : ℕ) - 1 : ℝ)⁻¹ = 0 ∧
      ∀ k : ℕ, Erdos124.sumsOfDistinctPowers 1 k = Set.univ := by
  refine ⟨fun _ _ h => Nat.add_lt_add_right h 1, by norm_num, by norm_num, ?_⟩
  intro k
  ext n
  simp only [Set.mem_univ, iff_true]
  exact ⟨Finset.Ico k (k + n), fun i hi => (Finset.mem_Ico.mp hi).1, by simp⟩

#print axioms original_statement_is_trivial
#print axioms missing_base_bound

end Erdos124Review

submission.summary: Corrected all three defects: added the base bound `2 ≤ d 0`, required summability of the reciprocal series, and required completeness for every positive exponent cutoff using the same sequence. Updated the docstring and linked Melfi’s Proposition 1; other declarations and attributes are unchanged. The requested compilation succeeds with only the permitted `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.

      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, n ∈ ∑ d ∈ D, sumsOfDistinctPowers d 0 := sorry

/--
Let $k \ne 0$ and $3\leq d_1 < d_2 < \cdots < d_r$ be integers of gcd equal to $1$ such that
$$\sum_{1 \le i \le r}\frac 1{d_i - 1} \ge 1.$$

where $c_i \in \{0, 1\}$ and $a_i$ is divisible by $d_i ^ k$ and has only the digits $0, 1$ when

Conjectured by Burr, Erdős, Graham, and Li [BEGL96]
-/

    ∀ k ≠ 0, ∀ D : Finset ℕ, (∀ d ∈ D, 3 ≤ d) → 1 ≤ ∑ d ∈ D, (d - 1 : ℚ)⁻¹ → D.gcd id = 1 →
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, n ∈ ∑ d ∈ D, sumsOfDistinctPowers d k := by
  sorry

/--
All sufficiently large integers can be written as $a + b + c$, where $a$, $b$, and $c$ are
divisible by $3$, $4$, and $7$ respectively, and after division by that base have only the

-/

lemma erdos124.ne_zero_three_four_seven :
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      n ∈ sumsOfDistinctPowers 3 1 + sumsOfDistinctPowers 4 1 + sumsOfDistinctPowers 7 1 :=

/--
Let $3\leq d_1 < d_2 < \cdots < d_r$ be integers such that all sufficiently large integers can be
written as a sum of the shape $\sum_i c_ia_i$ where $c_i \in \{0, 1\}$ and $a_i$ has only the digits
$0, 1$ when written in base $d_i$. Then
$$\sum_{1 \le i \le r}\frac 1{d_i - 1} \ge 1.$$

Reported by Burr, Erdős, Graham, and Li [BEGL96] as an observation of Pomerance
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/arex1337/formal-conjectures-proofs/blob/3b7d581c75fd00e482deabfb20675cf3ccfaf49f/Erdos124/Converse.lean"]

For any $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists an infinite sequence $2 \le d_0 < d_1 < \dots$ whose

  sorry

end Erdos124
